messages:
Felix Schneider: pulling folks in for quick gut check on perf-canary dashboard layout before i open the PR in observability-pack. goals: 1) per-model view that's usable oncall, 2) a heatmap/overview to spot regressions fast, 3) drill-downs, and 4) deploy annotations (runtime + canary runner) so pages are correlateable. thoughts?

Felix Schneider: current draft layout:
- Overview: heatmap = model x region with cell = p95 latency %Δ vs baseline (last 7d median), and second heatmap for tokens/sec %Δ
- Model detail: 4 panels: p95 latency timeseries, tokens/sec timeseries, sample_count, error rate
- Slice breakdown: table by gpu_sku + runtime_build + scheduler_mode with last 30m and last 6h deltas
- Links: runbook + incident-bot thread template

Logan Wright: +1 on starting with heatmap. but careful: model x region x gpu can get too busy if we show too many dims at once. overview should be stable even if a sku disappears.

Thomas Baird: yeah pls don’t put gpu_sku as an axis on the main heatmap. cardinality blowups aside, it also makes it unreadable oncall.

Nadia Rahman: for the model detail page, can we make the default filter pinned to `source=perf-canary` and `request_class=canary-safe` so we don’t accidentally pull in prod traffic? also can we show streaming vs non-streaming as a toggle.

Felix Schneider: yep, everything is scoped to `traffic_source="perf-canary"` (or whatever final label is) and a dashboard variable for `mode` = {streaming, non_streaming, all}.

Caleb Johnson: deploy annotations: do we already have a metric/event stream for runtime deploys we can query, or are we faking it with a time series label change? grafana annotations are easiest if we have something like `redwood_deploy_event{service="runtime", region="us-east", git_sha="...", runtime_build="..."} 1`.

Logan Wright: telemetry side: we can emit a “deploy marker” as a gauge=1 for ~10m after deploy. Connor’s team already does this for api-gateway. we can reuse that pattern.

Connor O'Brien: (lurking) yep we have a deploy marker generator in release-engineering. for runtime it’s not fully wired yet but easy. fields we can guarantee:
- service (runtime / perf-canary-runner)
- region
- runtime_version (semver-ish)
- git_sha
- build_id
we can also attach “rollout_phase” if needed.

Allison Grant: please use the standard annotation schema from observability-standards:
- label keys: `service`, `region`, `git_sha`, `version`
- avoid custom keys unless there’s a clear need
also: annotations should be queryable without joining (grafana annotation queries are limited).

Felix Schneider: ok so standard keys. question: runtime has both `runtime_build` and `git_sha` in our perf canary metrics. for annotation should we use `version`=runtime_version and `git_sha` and call it a day?

Nadia Rahman: yes. `runtime_build` as a dashboard variable is still useful for slicing metrics, but annotation can be a lightweight marker.

Thomas Baird: +1. keep annotation low-card.

Marissa Cole: from a “rollouts” POV: can we also annotate canary runner changes? we’ll be tuning workload + baseline logic and that will otherwise look like regressions.

Felix Schneider: was planning to add a second annotation query (service=perf-canary-runner). it’ll show up as a different color/line.

Caleb Johnson: 👀 make sure we can differentiate in legend/text. oncall should know whether a change came from runtime rollout or from canary code/config.

Felix Schneider: yep: annotation text template:
`[runtime] v${version} (${git_sha:0:7})` and `[canary-runner] v${version} (${git_sha:0:7})`.

Grafana Bot: Reminder: Annotation text templating supports label interpolation but not substring functions in OSS mode. You may need to include a pre-truncated `git_sha_short` label if you want 7-char.

Felix Schneider: lol thanks bot. ok we’ll include full sha or add sha_short at emission time.

Connor O'Brien: we can emit `git_sha_short` on deploy markers easily.

Logan Wright: on drill-downs: pls add click-through from heatmap cell -> model detail with region preselected.

Felix Schneider: yep. heatmap cell link goes to model dashboard with vars: model=${__data.fields.model} region=${__data.fields.region}

Nadia Rahman: what about showing baseline? oncall keeps asking “regression vs what”. can we have a panel that shows baseline value alongside current?

Felix Schneider: i can add a small “stat” row:
- current p95 (last 30m)
- baseline p95 (7d median)
- delta
same for tokens/sec.

Thomas Baird: for baseline, make sure query doesn’t explode. prefer precomputed baseline series if possible; otherwise use recording rules.

Logan Wright: we already have recording rules from ENG-2846 plan. but in the interim we can query `baseline_p95_ms` metric if/when runner publishes it. if not available, fallback to medians is ok but keep window fixed.

Allison Grant: also want a “data quality” block:
- sample_count
- % dropped labels
- outlier filter rate (if we’re excluding nodes)
so we can quickly identify false positives.

Felix Schneider: +1. i’ll add:
- `canary_requests_total` (last 30m)
- `canary_samples_used_total` vs `canary_samples_dropped_total`
- `canary_outlier_drops_total`

Caleb Johnson: deploy annotations: do we want to annotate runtime *config* flips too? e.g., scheduler_mode pinning changes or enabling/disabling an experimental heuristic.

Nadia Rahman: ideally yes but only if it’s common + reliable. otherwise we end up with a wall of markers.

Connor O'Brien: we can annotate “release event” only. config flips that are not tied to release train won’t show unless we emit markers from the config system. not in scope for phase 1.

Marissa Cole: agree, keep v1 simple. as long as the alert payload includes scheduler_mode + kernel id etc, oncall can triage.

Felix Schneider: ok, summarizing decisions:
1) Overview dashboard = 2 heatmaps (p95 Δ, tok/sec Δ) model x region. no gpu axis.
2) Click-through heatmap -> model detail with region preselected.
3) Model detail includes baseline/current stats + data quality row.
4) Slice breakdown table by gpu_sku/runtime_build/scheduler_mode on model detail page (not overview).
5) Annotations: two queries (runtime + canary-runner) using standard keys + `git_sha_short`.

Felix Schneider: i’ll post PR later today (observability-pack#844 style) with screenshots.

Logan Wright: :thumbsup: when you open the PR, tag @Nadia Rahman and @Thomas Baird for query/cardinality review.

Thomas Baird: +1 tag me. also please include the exact label filters in the PR description so we can sanity check.

Felix Schneider: will do.

deploy-bot: Deploy marker pipeline update (staging): enabled deploy events for service=runtime. Labels: service, region, version, git_sha, git_sha_short. ETA prod: pending approval from release-eng.

Caleb Johnson: nice. can we get perf-canary-runner too?

Connor O'Brien: yep, same mechanism. i’ll wire it once the runner has version tagging consistent.

Felix Schneider: perfect. closing loop once PR is up.
